Questions
Before you ask
The short version: it is free, it is independent, and it always shows you the source.
Is this legal advice?
No. constitution.ng explains what the Constitution says and shows you the exact section. If you are facing a court case, an arrest or a dispute, speak to a lawyer or the Legal Aid Council. Bring the sections you found here with you.
Is it free?
Yes. Asking questions, finding sections and reading the full Constitution are free. There is no paid plan.
Do I need an account?
No. You can ask and read as a guest. Create an account only if you want your conversations to follow you to another device.
Is this the current Constitution?
It is the 1999 Constitution as published in 2004. Amendments passed after that are not included yet, so a section may have changed since. Every answer tells you this so you can check before you rely on it.
Can I ask in Pidgin?
Yes. Ask the way you would say it, in English or Pidgin, and we will find the section. Answers are written in plain English, and the official wording is always the English text.
How do you choose the section?
Your question is matched against every section, using both the words you typed and what you mean. Citations come from the text itself, never guessed, and every answer lists the sections it used so you can read them yourself.
Can I quote an answer?
Yes. Copy any answer with its citations, or save the sections you need. Quote the official wording, not the explanation, when accuracy matters.
Is this a government website?
No. constitution.ng is independent. It is not published by, or connected to, the National Assembly or any government body.
